title: Broken phase
intro:
Each row of the table is one operator of the renormalised action after the shift H→Hv+φ, in the mass basis, with the operators of the unbroken phase from which it descends.

The broken phase is not renormalised separately. Its action is the renormalised action of the unbroken phase with the Higgs doublet shifted, H→Hv+φ, where Hv is the constant doublet with lower component v2, in the same linear gauge at ξ=1; no input from an Rξ gauge is used. The vacuum value v is defined at the tree-level minimum of the potential written with the MS-bar parameters, m2=−λ⁢v2; tadpole graphs are kept, and the singular counterterm contains a tadpole term. The masses MW, MZ, Mh and mk are tree-level MS-bar masses, not pole masses.

No loop calculation beyond those of the unbroken phase enters: every coefficient below descends from an operator of the unbroken phase, and the Exposé of a term shows the graphs of its parent operators. The fields are the mass eigenstates; the massive fermions have sterile partners, which change their propagator but not the counterterms. Apart from a hand check of the λ2 part of the tadpole pole, the only broken-phase loop calculation of the report is that of the fermion-loop two-point functions of the photon, of Z–photon mixing and of the gluon at zero momentum; it confirms that these bosons stay massless once the finite restoring terms are included.

The 370 terms are derived, not typed: the substitution H→Hv+φ and the rotation to the mass basis are applied to each operator of the unbroken catalogue (every SU(2) index in components), equal operators are collected, and each term lists its parents in the unbroken phase with the factor and the power of v with which they contribute. Terms that do not involve the Higgs doublet have the kind “unchanged by the shift”; they are the unbroken terms written in the mass basis.

overview.title: The broken phase as a change of variable
overview.text:
The renormalised action of the broken phase is the renormalised action of the unbroken phase, Sren=S0+δS(1)+ΔSST(1), written in the variable φ=H−Hv, with Φ′ all other fields and sources (report Eq. (521)). This is exact: the shift by the constant doublet Hv is a change of variable, the counterterms are local polynomials in H, and the linear gauge fixing does not depend on H, so the Slavnov–Taylor operator keeps its form and 𝐬φ=𝑖⁢𝛚(Hv+φ). No loop calculation beyond those of the unbroken phase enters, and no input from an Rξ gauge is used.

Every term of the table below was obtained by applying this substitution to the operators of the unbroken catalogue and collecting equal operators; its coefficients are sums of the parents' coefficients times exact factors. The table has 370 terms: 1 of kind “tadpole”, 10 of kind “mass”, 5 of kind “mixing”, 3 of kind “kinetic”, 61 of kind “interaction”, 24 of kind “source”, 37 of kind “evanescent”, 229 of kind “unchanged by the shift”. Field-independent constants (the value of the potential at Hv) are omitted.

overview.title: Shift and vacuum value
overview.text: Hv has the upper component 0 and the lower component v2; the fluctuation has the components φ1=G+ and φ2=h+𝑖⁢G02, with h, G0 real and G−=G+* (report Eq. (524)). The vacuum value is defined at the minimum of the tree-level potential written with the MS-bar parameters, m2=−λ⁢v2 with m2 negative (Eq. (523)): v is a function of m2 and λ, is not renormalised, and the tadpole graphs are kept. Every coefficient below uses this condition.

overview.title: Field basis: rotation of the gauge sector
overview.text: With cW=gg2+g′2, sW=g′g2+g′2 and e=g⁢sW=g′⁢cW (report Eq. (525)): Aμγ=sW⁢Wμ3+cW⁢Bμ, Wμ+=(Wμ1−𝑖⁢Wμ2)2 and Wμ−=(Wμ1+𝑖⁢Wμ2)2 (Eq. (526)). The same rotation, with the renormalised angle, is applied to the ghosts, antighosts, auxiliary fields and the sources ρaμ and ζa. The report does not rotate the fermion sources and the Higgs source; they appear in their SU(2) components, for example R‾Q1 and σ2†. The coefficients below are written with g, g′, cW, sW and e in whichever equivalent form is shortest.

overview.title: Fermion mass eigenstates and sterile partners
overview.text: The mass eigenstates are Dirac fields built from the physical components, with sterile partners built from the sterile ones (report Eq. (530)): u′=PRQ1+PLU, d=PLQ2+PRD, d′=PRQ2+PLD, e=PLL2+PRE, e′=PRL2+PLE and ν=L1, where Q1, Q2 are the upper and lower SU(2) components of the doublet. Mass terms, Yukawa and gauge couplings contain physical components only; the sterile partners appear only in the kinetic terms, through the evanescent terms 𝑖⁢u‾γˆμ∂μu′ and 𝑖⁢u′‾γˆμ∂μu.

overview.title: Tree-level masses

math.text: ℒ_{mass}=M_W² W^+_μ W^{−μ}+1/2 M_Z² Z_μ Z^μ−1/2 M_h² h h−Σ_fm_f f̅ f

overview.text: The gauge-boson mass terms come from (DμHv)†DμHv, a mass matrix ℳb⁢a2=Hv†{𝒯Ha,𝒯Hb}Hv over the four SU(2)×U(1) components, with eigenvalues MW2 (twice), MZ2 and 0 (photon) (report Eq. (528)). The tree-level masses are MW=g⁢v2, MZ=MWcW, Mh2=2⁢λ⁢v2 and mk=yk⁢v2 for k = u, d, e (Eq. (529)); the photon, the gluon, the neutrino, the Goldstone fields and all ghosts are massless in this gauge. They are MS-bar masses at the tree-level minimum, not pole masses. In the table the corresponding terms are written with g, v, yk, λ; their remarks give the identification.

overview.title: Gauge–Goldstone mixing

math.text: ℒ_{mix}=M_Z Z_μ ∂^μ G^0+𝑖 M_W (W^−_μ ∂^μ G^+−W^+_μ ∂^μ G^−)

overview.text: Because the gauge fixing is linear and does not depend on H, the tree-level mixing between gauge and Goldstone fields stays in the quadratic action (report Eq. (532)); it enters the propagators, which have mixed gauge–Goldstone parts and double poles at k2=0 (Eq. (537)). The singular counterterm adds a photon–Goldstone term, and the finite counterterm changes the mixing by −13Y˜ times its tree value (Eq. (564)).

overview.title: Tadpole
overview.text: The tree-level tadpole −v⁢h⁢(λ⁢v2+m2) vanishes by the vacuum condition. The singular counterterm contains the tadpole term −v⁢h⁢δT (report Eq. (550), Eq. (551)), which cancels the pole of the one-loop tadpole; here v⁢δT=116π21ϵ⁢v3⁢(−λ⁢CH−Y4+3⁢G416+6⁢λ2) with CH=2⁢MW2+MZ2v2, Y4=4⁢(3⁢mu4+3⁢md4+me4)v4 and G4=16⁢(2⁢MW4+MZ4)v4 (Eq. (542)). The Goldstone mass counterterm equals δT. Only the λ2 part of the tadpole pole was checked in the report; the finite one-loop tadpole is not computed there. The finite restoring counterterm gives no tadpole.

overview.title: How the counterterms follow
overview.text: The singular counterterm is the first-order term of S0 in the bare quantities, now at H=Hv+φ: v is not renormalised, the rotation uses the renormalised g and g′, and the gauge fixing is not renormalised (report Section 5.4.4). The v-dependent mass, mixing and tadpole counterterms therefore follow from the unbroken-phase constants of Table 57. The finite restoring counterterm is ΔSST(1) at H=Hv+φ (Section 5.4.5): its H-dependent coefficients are purely Yukawa, so after the shift its terms with Hv are proportional to fermion masses squared; no coefficient is recomputed. Under (N1) there is no finite counterterm for the fermion masses, the Yukawa vertices, the scalar potential or the tadpole.

overview.text: For the pair u, u′ the quadratic Lagrangian has the kinetic matrix with the entries −mu+/p‾ and /p‾ on the diagonal and /pˆ off the diagonal (report Eq. (538)); the propagator is 𝑖 times its inverse, whose physical block Sphys is shown (with mf=mu). Its denominator depends on p2 and p‾2 separately and is not d-dimensionally covariant; at vanishing hatted momentum, where external fermions live, it reduces to the standard mf+/p‾p‾2−mf2. The other blocks are mf⁢/p‾/pˆ+p2⁢/pˆ(p2)2−mf2⁢p‾2, −mf⁢/p‾/pˆ+p2⁢/pˆ(p2)2−mf2⁢p‾2 and mf⁢pˆ2+(p2−mf2)⁢/p‾(p2)2−mf2⁢p‾2. The neutrino has the massless propagator. The counterterms are unaffected: the mass can be treated as a two-point insertion on massless propagators, so poles and the finite breaking are polynomials in the masses (Section 5.5.2).

rules.note: The finite part is the vertex function of the four-dimensional operator: its metrics and momenta are barred.

terms.remarks: Not changed by the shift; written in the mass basis. It is the image of Cubic SU(2) gauge vertex (factor g⁢cW): each coefficient is the sum of the parents' coefficients times these factors. The tree-level and singular coefficients multiply the d-dimensional operator shown; the finite coefficient multiplies its four-dimensional form, in which all fields, derivatives and metrics are barred.

rules.note: The finite part is the vertex function of the four-dimensional operator: its metrics and momenta are barred.

terms.remarks: Not changed by the shift; written in the mass basis. It is the image of Cubic SU(2) gauge vertex (factor e): each coefficient is the sum of the parents' coefficients times these factors. The tree-level and singular coefficients multiply the d-dimensional operator shown; the finite coefficient multiplies its four-dimensional form, in which all fields, derivatives and metrics are barred.

rules.note: The finite part is the vertex function of the four-dimensional operator: its metrics and momenta are barred.

terms.remarks: Not changed by the shift; written in the mass basis. It is the image of Four-W operator (Wᴵ·Wᴶ)² (factor g4): each coefficient is the sum of the parents' coefficients times these factors. The tree-level and singular coefficients multiply the d-dimensional operator shown; the finite coefficient multiplies its four-dimensional form, in which all fields, derivatives and metrics are barred.

rules.note: The finite part is the vertex function of the four-dimensional operator: its metrics and momenta are barred.

terms.remarks: Not changed by the shift; written in the mass basis. It is the image of Four-W operator (Wᴵ·Wᴶ)² (factor g4⁢cW⁢sW); W–B quartic operator (Wᴵ·B)² (factor g4⁢cW⁢sW⁢(12−121cW2)): each coefficient is the sum of the parents' coefficients times these factors. The tree-level and singular coefficients multiply the d-dimensional operator shown; the finite coefficient multiplies its four-dimensional form, in which all fields, derivatives and metrics are barred.

rules.note: The finite part is the vertex function of the four-dimensional operator: its metrics and momenta are barred.

terms.remarks: Not changed by the shift; written in the mass basis. It is the image of Four-W operator (Wᴵ·Wᴶ)² (factor 4⁢g4⁢sW2); W–B quartic operator (Wᴵ·B)² (factor 2⁢g4⁢sW2): each coefficient is the sum of the parents' coefficients times these factors. The tree-level and singular coefficients multiply the d-dimensional operator shown; the finite coefficient multiplies its four-dimensional form, in which all fields, derivatives and metrics are barred.

rules.note: The finite part is the vertex function of the four-dimensional operator: its metrics and momenta are barred.

terms.remarks: Image under the shift of Higgs–W–W seagull term (factor 14g2⁢v2, order v2): each coefficient is the sum of the parents' coefficients times these factors. With the tree-level masses of the report (Eq. (529)) the tree-level coefficient is MW2. The tree-level and singular coefficients multiply the d-dimensional operator shown; the finite coefficient multiplies its four-dimensional form, in which all fields, derivatives and metrics are barred. The graphs shown are those of the parents in the unbroken phase; broken-phase graphs are not drawn. Pole parts and the finite breaking of the broken phase are the unbroken-phase ones with external H legs set to Hv at zero momentum (report Section 5.5.1, point 2).

terms.remarks: Image under the shift of Higgs–W–W seagull term (factor 14g2⁢v2⁢cW2, order v2); Higgs–W–B seagull term (factor 12e2⁢v2, order v2); Higgs–B–B seagull term (factor 14g′2⁢v2⁢sW2, order v2): each coefficient is the sum of the parents' coefficients times these factors. With the tree-level masses of the report (Eq. (529)) the tree-level coefficient is MZ2. The tree-level and singular coefficients multiply the d-dimensional operator shown; the finite coefficient multiplies its four-dimensional form, in which all fields, derivatives and metrics are barred. The graphs shown are those of the parents in the unbroken phase; broken-phase graphs are not drawn. Pole parts and the finite breaking of the broken phase are the unbroken-phase ones with external H legs set to Hv at zero momentum (report Section 5.5.1, point 2).

rules.note: The finite part is the vertex function of the four-dimensional operator: its metrics and momenta are barred.

terms.remarks: Image under the shift of Higgs–W–W seagull term (factor 14e2⁢v2, order v2); Higgs–W–B seagull term (factor −12e2⁢v2, order v2); Higgs–B–B seagull term (factor 14e2⁢v2, order v2): each coefficient is the sum of the parents' coefficients times these factors. The finite photon mass-like term is required: at one loop and zero momentum the fermion loops of the regularised theory give the photon a finite mass term, and this counterterm cancels it exactly (report Section 5.4.6, Eq. (575); checked there also through the Slavnov–Taylor identity of the ghost–photon legs). There is no singular photon mass term. The graphs shown are those of the parents in the unbroken phase; broken-phase graphs are not drawn. Pole parts and the finite breaking of the broken phase are the unbroken-phase ones with external H legs set to Hv at zero momentum (report Section 5.5.1, point 2).

terms.remarks: Image under the shift of Higgs–W–W seagull term (factor 14g2⁢v2⁢cW⁢sW, order v2); Higgs–W–B seagull term (factor 14g2⁢v2⁢cW⁢sW⁢(−2+1cW2), order v2); Higgs–B–B seagull term (factor −14g′2⁢v2⁢cW⁢sW, order v2): each coefficient is the sum of the parents' coefficients times these factors. Z–photon mixing of mass type. The fermion-loop part of the Z–photon two-point function vanishes at zero momentum once the finite term is included (report Section 5.4.6); the singular term comes from bosonic loops. The tree-level and singular coefficients multiply the d-dimensional operator shown; the finite coefficient multiplies its four-dimensional form, in which all fields, derivatives and metrics are barred. The graphs shown are those of the parents in the unbroken phase; broken-phase graphs are not drawn. Pole parts and the finite breaking of the broken phase are the unbroken-phase ones with external H legs set to Hv at zero momentum (report Section 5.5.1, point 2).

terms.remarks: Not changed by the shift; written in the mass basis. The operator collects the two chirality projections of one bilinear. terms.remarks: The operator collects the two chirality projections of one bilinear. The PR projection is the image under the shift of Up-quark Yukawa term −Ou (part of Qyu+) (factor −v2, order v); the PL projection is the image under the shift of Up-quark Yukawa term −Ou† (part of Qyu+) (factor −v2, order v). For each projection the sum of its parents' coefficients times these factors is the coefficient of the operator shown; the two projections have the same coefficient. With the tree-level masses of the report (Eq. (529)) the tree-level coefficient is −mu. Only the physical components couple to the mass; the sterile partner enters the propagator through the evanescent kinetic term (report Eq. (538)). Under (N1) there is no finite fermion mass counterterm. The graphs shown are those of the parents in the unbroken phase; broken-phase graphs are not drawn. Pole parts and the finite breaking of the broken phase are the unbroken-phase ones with external H legs set to Hv at zero momentum (report Section 5.5.1, point 2).

terms.remarks: The operator collects the two chirality projections of one bilinear. The PR projection is the image under the shift of Electron Yukawa term −Oe (part of Qye+) (factor −v2, order v); the PL projection is the image under the shift of Electron Yukawa term −Oe† (part of Qye+) (factor −v2, order v). For each projection the sum of its parents' coefficients times these factors is the coefficient of the operator shown; the two projections have the same coefficient. With the tree-level masses of the report (Eq. (529)) the tree-level coefficient is −me. Only the physical components couple to the mass; the sterile partner enters the propagator through the evanescent kinetic term (report Eq. (538)). Under (N1) there is no finite fermion mass counterterm. The graphs shown are those of the parents in the unbroken phase; broken-phase graphs are not drawn. Pole parts and the finite breaking of the broken phase are the unbroken-phase ones with external H legs set to Hv at zero momentum (report Section 5.5.1, point 2).

terms.remarks: Image under the shift of Higgs mass term (factor v, order v); Higgs quartic self-coupling (factor v3, order v3): each coefficient is the sum of the parents' coefficients times these factors. The coefficients use the vacuum condition m2=−λ⁢v2. The tree-level tadpole −v⁢h⁢(λ⁢v2+m2) vanishes by the vacuum condition m2=−λ⁢v2. The singular tadpole term is −v⁢h⁢δT with δT=λ⁢v2⁢δZH+δm2+v2⁢δλ (report Eq. (551)); it cancels the pole of the one-loop tadpole, whose tadpole graphs are kept. The report checked only the λ2 part of this pole by hand, and it does not compute the finite one-loop tadpole. The finite restoring counterterm gives no tadpole. The graphs shown are those of the parents in the unbroken phase; broken-phase graphs are not drawn. Pole parts and the finite breaking of the broken phase are the unbroken-phase ones with external H legs set to Hv at zero momentum (report Section 5.5.1, point 2).

The coefficients use the vacuum condition m2=−λ⁢v2. The Goldstone fields are massless at tree level in this gauge. The mass counterterm equals δT, as required by the relation between the Goldstone two-point function at zero momentum and the tadpole once tadpoles are included (report Section 5.4.4). The graphs shown are those of the parents in the unbroken phase; broken-phase graphs are not drawn. Pole parts and the finite breaking of the broken phase are the unbroken-phase ones with external H legs set to Hv at zero momentum (report Section 5.5.1, point 2).

terms.remarks: Image under the shift of Higgs mass term (factor 1); Higgs quartic self-coupling (factor v2, order v2): each coefficient is the sum of the parents' coefficients times these factors. The coefficients use the vacuum condition m2=−λ⁢v2. The Goldstone fields are massless at tree level in this gauge. The mass counterterm equals δT, as required by the relation between the Goldstone two-point function at zero momentum and the tadpole (report Section 5.4.4). The graphs shown are those of the parents in the unbroken phase; broken-phase graphs are not drawn. Pole parts and the finite breaking of the broken phase are the unbroken-phase ones with external H legs set to Hv at zero momentum (report Section 5.5.1, point 2).

terms.remarks: Image under the shift of Higgs–SU(2) current term (factor i2g⁢v, order v): each coefficient is the sum of the parents' coefficients times these factors. With the tree-level masses of the report (Eq. (529)) the tree-level coefficient is −𝑖⁢MW. The tree-level gauge–Goldstone mixing remains because the gauge fixing is linear (report Eq. (532)). The finite part is −13Y˜ times the tree-level mixing (Eq. (564)). The tree-level and singular coefficients multiply the d-dimensional operator shown; the finite coefficient multiplies its four-dimensional form, in which all fields, derivatives and metrics are barred. The graphs shown are those of the parents in the unbroken phase; broken-phase graphs are not drawn. Pole parts and the finite breaking of the broken phase are the unbroken-phase ones with external H legs set to Hv at zero momentum (report Section 5.5.1, point 2).

rules.note: The finite part is the vertex function of the four-dimensional operator: its metrics and momenta are barred.

terms.remarks: Image under the shift of Higgs–SU(2) current term (factor −i2g⁢v, order v): each coefficient is the sum of the parents' coefficients times these factors. With the tree-level masses of the report (Eq. (529)) the tree-level coefficient is 𝑖⁢MW. The tree-level gauge–Goldstone mixing remains because the gauge fixing is linear (report Eq. (532)). The finite part is −13Y˜ times the tree-level mixing (Eq. (564)). The tree-level and singular coefficients multiply the d-dimensional operator shown; the finite coefficient multiplies its four-dimensional form, in which all fields, derivatives and metrics are barred. The graphs shown are those of the parents in the unbroken phase; broken-phase graphs are not drawn. Pole parts and the finite breaking of the broken phase are the unbroken-phase ones with external H legs set to Hv at zero momentum (report Section 5.5.1, point 2).

terms.remarks: Image under the shift of Higgs–SU(2) current term (factor −12g⁢v⁢cW, order v); Higgs–hypercharge current term (factor −12g′⁢v⁢sW, order v): each coefficient is the sum of the parents' coefficients times these factors. With the tree-level masses of the report (Eq. (529)) the tree-level coefficient is MZ. The tree-level gauge–Goldstone mixing remains because the gauge fixing is linear; only an H-dependent gauge fixing such as the R_ξ gauge, which is not used, would cancel it. The finite part is −13Y˜ times the tree-level mixing (report Eq. (564)). The tree-level and singular coefficients multiply the d-dimensional operator shown; the finite coefficient multiplies its four-dimensional form, in which all fields, derivatives and metrics are barred. The graphs shown are those of the parents in the unbroken phase; broken-phase graphs are not drawn. Pole parts and the finite breaking of the broken phase are the unbroken-phase ones with external H legs set to Hv at zero momentum (report Section 5.5.1, point 2).

rules.note: The finite part is the vertex function of the four-dimensional operator: its metrics and momenta are barred.

terms.remarks: Image under the shift of Higgs–SU(2) current term (factor g⁢cW); Higgs–hypercharge current term (factor g′⁢sW): each coefficient is the sum of the parents' coefficients times these factors. The tree-level and singular coefficients multiply the d-dimensional operator shown; the finite coefficient multiplies its four-dimensional form, in which all fields, derivatives and metrics are barred. The graphs shown are those of the parents in the unbroken phase; broken-phase graphs are not drawn. Pole parts and the finite breaking of the broken phase are the unbroken-phase ones with external H legs set to Hv at zero momentum (report Section 5.5.1, point 2).

rules.note: The finite part is the vertex function of the four-dimensional operator: its metrics and momenta are barred.

terms.remarks: Image under the shift of Higgs–SU(2) current term (factor g⁢cW); Higgs–hypercharge current term (factor −g′⁢sW): each coefficient is the sum of the parents' coefficients times these factors. The tree-level and singular coefficients multiply the d-dimensional operator shown; the finite coefficient multiplies its four-dimensional form, in which all fields, derivatives and metrics are barred. The graphs shown are those of the parents in the unbroken phase; broken-phase graphs are not drawn. Pole parts and the finite breaking of the broken phase are the unbroken-phase ones with external H legs set to Hv at zero momentum (report Section 5.5.1, point 2).

The tree-level and singular coefficients multiply the d-dimensional operator shown; the finite coefficient multiplies its four-dimensional form, in which all fields, derivatives and metrics are barred. The graphs shown are those of the parents in the unbroken phase; broken-phase graphs are not drawn. Pole parts and the finite breaking of the broken phase are the unbroken-phase ones with external H legs set to Hv at zero momentum (report Section 5.5.1, point 2).

rules.note: The finite part is the vertex function of the four-dimensional operator: its metrics and momenta are barred.

terms.remarks: Image under the shift of Higgs–W–W seagull term (factor 12g2⁢v, order v): each coefficient is the sum of the parents' coefficients times these factors. The tree-level and singular coefficients multiply the d-dimensional operator shown; the finite coefficient multiplies its four-dimensional form, in which all fields, derivatives and metrics are barred. The graphs shown are those of the parents in the unbroken phase; broken-phase graphs are not drawn. Pole parts and the finite breaking of the broken phase are the unbroken-phase ones with external H legs set to Hv at zero momentum (report Section 5.5.1, point 2).

terms.remarks: Image under the shift of Higgs–W–W seagull term (factor 14g2⁢v⁢cW2, order v); Higgs–W–B seagull term (factor 12e2⁢v, order v); Higgs–B–B seagull term (factor 14g′2⁢v⁢sW2, order v): each coefficient is the sum of the parents' coefficients times these factors. The tree-level and singular coefficients multiply the d-dimensional operator shown; the finite coefficient multiplies its four-dimensional form, in which all fields, derivatives and metrics are barred. The graphs shown are those of the parents in the unbroken phase; broken-phase graphs are not drawn. Pole parts and the finite breaking of the broken phase are the unbroken-phase ones with external H legs set to Hv at zero momentum (report Section 5.5.1, point 2).

terms.remarks: Image under the shift of Higgs–W–W seagull term (factor 18g2⁢cW2); Higgs–W–B seagull term (factor 14e2); Higgs–B–B seagull term (factor 18g′2⁢sW2): each coefficient is the sum of the parents' coefficients times these factors. The tree-level and singular coefficients multiply the d-dimensional operator shown; the finite coefficient multiplies its four-dimensional form, in which all fields, derivatives and metrics are barred. The graphs shown are those of the parents in the unbroken phase; broken-phase graphs are not drawn. Pole parts and the finite breaking of the broken phase are the unbroken-phase ones with external H legs set to Hv at zero momentum (report Section 5.5.1, point 2).

terms.remarks: Image under the shift of Higgs–W–W seagull term (factor 14g2⁢cW2); Higgs–W–B seagull term (factor −12e2); Higgs–B–B seagull term (factor 14g′2⁢sW2): each coefficient is the sum of the parents' coefficients times these factors. The tree-level and singular coefficients multiply the d-dimensional operator shown; the finite coefficient multiplies its four-dimensional form, in which all fields, derivatives and metrics are barred. The graphs shown are those of the parents in the unbroken phase; broken-phase graphs are not drawn. Pole parts and the finite breaking of the broken phase are the unbroken-phase ones with external H legs set to Hv at zero momentum (report Section 5.5.1, point 2).

terms.remarks: Image under the shift of Higgs–W–W seagull term (factor 14g2⁢cW⁢sW); Higgs–W–B seagull term (factor 14g2⁢cW⁢sW⁢(−2+1cW2)); Higgs–B–B seagull term (factor −14g2⁢sW3cW): each coefficient is the sum of the parents' coefficients times these factors. The tree-level and singular coefficients multiply the d-dimensional operator shown; the finite coefficient multiplies its four-dimensional form, in which all fields, derivatives and metrics are barred. The graphs shown are those of the parents in the unbroken phase; broken-phase graphs are not drawn. Pole parts and the finite breaking of the broken phase are the unbroken-phase ones with external H legs set to Hv at zero momentum (report Section 5.5.1, point 2).

terms.remarks: Image under the shift of Higgs–W–B seagull term (factor −12e2cW): each coefficient is the sum of the parents' coefficients times these factors. The tree-level and singular coefficients multiply the d-dimensional operator shown; the finite coefficient multiplies its four-dimensional form, in which all fields, derivatives and metrics are barred. The graphs shown are those of the parents in the unbroken phase; broken-phase graphs are not drawn. Pole parts and the finite breaking of the broken phase are the unbroken-phase ones with external H legs set to Hv at zero momentum (report Section 5.5.1, point 2).

terms.remarks: Image under the shift of Higgs–W–B seagull term (factor 12g2⁢sW): each coefficient is the sum of the parents' coefficients times these factors. The tree-level and singular coefficients multiply the d-dimensional operator shown; the finite coefficient multiplies its four-dimensional form, in which all fields, derivatives and metrics are barred. The graphs shown are those of the parents in the unbroken phase; broken-phase graphs are not drawn. Pole parts and the finite breaking of the broken phase are the unbroken-phase ones with external H legs set to Hv at zero momentum (report Section 5.5.1, point 2).

terms.remarks: Image under the shift of Higgs–W–B seagull term (factor −12e2cW): each coefficient is the sum of the parents' coefficients times these factors. The tree-level and singular coefficients multiply the d-dimensional operator shown; the finite coefficient multiplies its four-dimensional form, in which all fields, derivatives and metrics are barred. The graphs shown are those of the parents in the unbroken phase; broken-phase graphs are not drawn. Pole parts and the finite breaking of the broken phase are the unbroken-phase ones with external H legs set to Hv at zero momentum (report Section 5.5.1, point 2).

terms.remarks: Image under the shift of Higgs–W–B seagull term (factor −12g2⁢sW): each coefficient is the sum of the parents' coefficients times these factors. The graphs shown are those of the parents in the unbroken phase; broken-phase graphs are not drawn. Pole parts and the finite breaking of the broken phase are the unbroken-phase ones with external H legs set to Hv at zero momentum (report Section 5.5.1, point 2).

terms.remarks: The operator collects the two chirality projections of one bilinear. The PR projection is the image under the shift of Up-quark Yukawa term −Ou (part of Qyu+) (factor 12); the PL projection is the image under the shift of Up-quark Yukawa term −Ou† (part of Qyu+) (factor 12). For each projection the sum of its parents' coefficients times these factors is the coefficient of the operator shown; the two projections have the same coefficient. The graphs shown are those of the parents in the unbroken phase; broken-phase graphs are not drawn. Pole parts and the finite breaking of the broken phase are the unbroken-phase ones with external H legs set to Hv at zero momentum (report Section 5.5.1, point 2).

terms.remarks: The operator collects the two chirality projections of one bilinear. The PR projection is the image under the shift of Down-quark Yukawa term −Od (part of Qyd+) (factor −12); the PL projection is the image under the shift of Down-quark Yukawa term −Od† (part of Qyd+) (factor −12). For each projection the sum of its parents' coefficients times these factors is the coefficient of the operator shown; the two projections have the same coefficient. The graphs shown are those of the parents in the unbroken phase; broken-phase graphs are not drawn. Pole parts and the finite breaking of the broken phase are the unbroken-phase ones with external H legs set to Hv at zero momentum (report Section 5.5.1, point 2).

terms.remarks: The operator collects the two chirality projections of one bilinear. The PR projection is the image under the shift of Down-quark Yukawa term −Od (part of Qyd+) (factor −12); the PL projection is the image under the shift of Down-quark Yukawa term −Od† (part of Qyd+) (factor −12). For each projection the sum of its parents' coefficients times these factors is the coefficient of the operator shown; the two projections have the same coefficient. The graphs shown are those of the parents in the unbroken phase; broken-phase graphs are not drawn. Pole parts and the finite breaking of the broken phase are the unbroken-phase ones with external H legs set to Hv at zero momentum (report Section 5.5.1, point 2).

terms.remarks: The operator collects the two chirality projections of one bilinear. The PR projection is the image under the shift of Electron Yukawa term −Oe (part of Qye+) (factor −12); the PL projection is the image under the shift of Electron Yukawa term −Oe† (part of Qye+) (factor −12). For each projection the sum of its parents' coefficients times these factors is the coefficient of the operator shown; the two projections have the same coefficient. The graphs shown are those of the parents in the unbroken phase; broken-phase graphs are not drawn. Pole parts and the finite breaking of the broken phase are the unbroken-phase ones with external H legs set to Hv at zero momentum (report Section 5.5.1, point 2).
